Tranf- ferences being but incidental to other actions, can be pro nounced by that inferior judge alone before whom the principal caule depended; but, where the reprefentatives of the deceafed live in another territory, it is the fupreme court which muft transfer. Obligations may be now regiltred fummarily after the creditor's death ; which be fore was not admitted, without a feparate proceeds of re giltration, to which the granter was necellarily to be made a party.<x_0.9082><y_0.1523><class_Text>

<x_0.0146><y_0.15>26. A process of wakening is likewise acceffory. An action is laid to fleep, when it lies over, not inflicted in for a year, in which cafe its effect is fufpended ; but even then it may, at any time within the years of prefeription, be revived or wakened by a fummons, in which the purfuer recites the laft lep of the procels, and concludes that it may be again carried on as if it had not been dif- continued. An action that stands upon any of the inner- houte rolls cannot fleep ; nor an action in which decree is pronounced, because it has got its full completion : Conféquently the decree may be extracted after the year, without the necessity of a wakening.<x_0.9072><y_0.332><class_Text>

<x_0.0137><y_0.3305>27. An action of tranfumpt falls under the fame clats. It is competent to thofe, who have a partial interest in writings that are not in their own cultody, against the poffeffors thereof, for exhibiting them, that they may be tranfumed for their behoof. Though the ordinary title in this proceeds be an obligation by the defender to grant tranfumpts to the purfuer, it is sufficient if the purfuer can show that he has an interelt in the writings ; but, in this cafe, he muft tranfume them on his own charges. Actions of tranfumpt may be purified before any judge-ordinary. After the writings to be tranfumed are exhibited, full duplicates are made out, collated, and figned, by one of the clerks of court, which are called tranfumpts, and are as effected as an extract from the register.<x_0.9062><y_0.5563><class_Text>

<x_0.0127><y_0.5555>28. Actions proceeded anciently upon brieves iffing from the chancery, directed to the judiciary or judge-or dinary, who tried the matter by a jury, upon whole verdict judgment was pronounced: And to this day, we retain certain brieves, as of _inquefl_, terce, ideotry, tutory, perambulation, and perhaps two or three others: But fummones were, immediately upon the initiation of the College of Jutice, introduced in the place of brieves. A fummons, when applied to actions purfued before the fiction, is a writ in the King’s name, iffuing from his fignet upon the purfuer’s complaint, authorifing meffengers to cite the defender to appear before the court, and make his defences ; with certification if he fail to appear, that decree will be pronounced againl him in terms of the certification of the fummons.<x_0.9053><y_0.7797><class_Text>

<x_0.0117><y_0.7789>29. The days indulged by law to a defender, between his citation and appearance, to prepare for his defence, are called _inducie legales_. If he is within the kingdom, twenty one and fix days, for the first and fecond diets of appearance, muft be allowed him for that purpose ; and if out of it, fixty and fifteen. Defenders relating in Orkney or Zetland mult be cited on forty days. In certain fummones which are priviledged, the _inducie_ are shortened: Spuilzies and ejections proceed on fifteen days ;<x_0.9043><y_0.9164><class_Text>
